prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (max 500 words)

Scope and funding
- Applies to Westminster; notes devolved differences.  
- Reprioritises about £5bn/year by: abolishing a central industry department and subsidies, cancelling ID cards, and redirecting Child Trust Fund money.  
- Single net tax rise: 50% rate on income above £100,000 to fund three pledges—abolish university tuition/top-up fees, provide free personal care, and cut local taxes.  
- Replace Council Tax with a Local Income Tax (typical household saving ~£450). National Audit Office to scrutinise budgets; simplify taxes and reduce debt risks.

Health and care
- Free personal care for elderly and disabled people.  
- Faster diagnosis via any suitable provider; expand scanning capacity, publish diagnostic waits.  
- Free eye/dental checks; widen prescription charge exemptions.  
- Recruit more clinicians; remove central targets; strengthen local accountability.  
- Reform NHS dentistry; personal care plans; stronger mental health safeguards; end age discrimination.  
- Prevention: school nutrition standards, restrict unhealthy food ads to children, healthy vending, clearer labelling; ban smoking in enclosed public places.

Education and skills
- Abolish tuition/top-up fees; grants for low-income students.  
- Use Child Trust Fund monies to cut class sizes (infant avg 20; junior 25); extend 8am–6pm provision; complete 3,500 Children’s Centres by 2010.  
- Ensure specialist teachers in core subjects; reduce high-stakes testing; strengthen discipline support.  
- Integrate academic/vocational pathways via a new diploma; close funding gaps for colleges; invest in facilities; maintain free school transport distances.  
- Green standards for new education buildings and value outdoor learning.

Crime, justice, borders
- 10,000 extra police funded by scrapping ID cards; complete 20,000 CSOs; cut police bureaucracy; target traffickers and acquisitive drug crime.  
- Community payback for non‑violent offenders; tougher action on disorder linked to alcohol.  
- Prisons focused on education, skills and work.  
- Create a UK Border Force; protect jury trial; use intercept evidence; any control orders judge‑led, time‑limited; repeal the 2005 regime.  
- Overhaul asylum with a dedicated agency; allow asylum seekers to work.  
- Single Equality Act; hate‑crime units; specialist Environmental Tribunal.

Economy, business, energy
- Keep fiscal rules; independent statistics; tackle misleading consumer credit.  
- Small business rate relief (up to £1,500); site-value rating; sunset clauses for regulations; single inspections; abolish the central industry department (savings reinvested).  
- Shift Climate Change Levy to a Carbon Tax; at least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; do not replace ageing nuclear plants.

Pensions, families, disability
- From 75: raise basic state pension (earnings-linked), removing means tests for ~1m; residency-based “citizen’s pension” from 75; Local Income Tax benefits 8/10 pensioners.  
- First-child maternity pay: minimum wage rate for six months.  
- Replace Child Support Agency with HMRC-led system plus tribunal.  
- £200 Winter Fuel Payment extended to severely disabled working-age people; allow insulation vouchers; bolster failed pension scheme compensation.

Housing, local services, culture
- Release public land for 100,000 affordable homes; reform VAT to favour reuse/brownfield; stamp duty threshold £150,000; planning control on second homes in hotspots.  
- Reduce inspections by merging into a single Audit Commission; protect post offices; restore Lottery independence; maintain universal postal pricing.

Transport
- Fewer, longer rail franchises tied to investment; fund station safety and key upgrades; promote rail freight and waterways.  
- Reform VED to reward low‑emission cars; expand congestion charging with upfront public transport investment; long‑term national road pricing to replace fuel duty/VED.  
- Free off‑peak local buses for pensioners/disabled; free rail discount cards for named groups.  
- Cautious on new roads; aviation: per‑aircraft charging, emissions trading; oppose new/expanded SE airports; protect lifeline routes.

Rural, environment, governance, international
- Fair trading duty with a Food Trade Inspector; faster CAP reform; Marine Act; Animal Protection Commission and modern welfare law; no commercial GM without safety assurance.  
- Zero-waste goal; 60% household recycling in seven years; sustainable planning and building rules.  
- War Powers Act; Civil Service Act; cut ministries/ministers; devolve powers; STV for elections; predominantly elected second chamber; votes at 16; stronger, more independent BBC regulator.  
- Iraq: support transition, strengthen Iraqi forces, aim to withdraw with UN mandate expiry.  
- EU reform; referendum on constitution; prepare to join euro when conditions met.  
- Defence: reallocate procurement (e.g., scale back Eurofighter tranche 3), maintain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing reductions; tighter arms export oversight.  
- Development: lift aid to 0.5% GNI by 2007/08 and 0.7% by 2011; end agricultural dumping; greener aid; lead on climate “contraction and convergence.”
